statements.says: The scripts move to Python, bottom up, one program and its test at a time: ticket-worktree, then land-ticket, then spec-loop.
fetch-origin moves with the first program, and its bash copy lives until the last one goes.
skillworks-preflight.sh stays bash for good.
node leaves the loop altogether, because it was there to read JSON and json is in Python's stdlib.
Every program the driver reaches goes through a Runner, injected the way the Clock is.
A separate, small set of tests starts the real binaries, so something still proves gh takes the arguments the driver builds.
.py joins source-files.
__pycache__, .venv, venv and site-packages join skip-folders in the same commit as .py joins source-files.
test-files gains *_test.py rather than *.test.py.
The doc comment check gains a docstring detector.
Determinism stays out of reach for Python, as it already is for bash, and closing that is a job of its own.
Every process Git Bash starts costs about 2.9 seconds, while native Python and PowerShell start the same program in 59 milliseconds.
The spec-loop bash test file runs 28 cases in 53 minutes, almost all of it process start-up tax rather than work.
A build session cannot run the suite inside the 600 second cap the Bash tool puts on a command, so it loses the result and polls for it.
The spec-loop script is 468 lines of bash carrying nineteen lines of JavaScript inside a string.
Earlier research had already picked Python over Node because Python starts .cmd files on Windows, can end a claude turn rather than only kill it, and reaches Job Objects from stdlib.
Speed was not among the research's three grounds, and it is the largest of the four.
The preflight stays bash because it tells a new machine whether it can run the loop, and cannot be written in the language it is checking for.
A Runner is needed because a test can no longer fake a program with a shell file on PATH, since Windows reads PATHEXT and ignores a shebang.
The skip-folders entries land with .py because the tree walk does not ask git, and a virtual environment arriving first would flood the check with folders named utils and helpers.
*_test.py is used because foo.test is not a name Python can import, and pytest could not collect the file.
The docstring detector is needed because Python writes docstrings by reflex, so doc-comments: false would be broken by the first file to land carrying one.
Leaving determinism out of reach for Python makes nothing worse, because the check filters on .cs before it reads the context list, and loop is not among the contexts it judges anyway.
Running the bash suite under WSL or in a container was rejected, because the scripts would be tested on Linux bash but run on Git Bash, where the MSYS_NO_PATHCONV workarounds exist only on Windows.
Running the bash suite under WSL or in a container was also rejected because it leaves the driver itself slow, since the real loop pays the same tax on every git, gh and claude it starts.
Cutting the number of spawns, such as copying one template repository per case, was rejected as too small, because the tax is spread through the suite rather than gathered in the fixture.
Node rather than Python was rejected, because Node only half fits the rules today, and half fitting is what keeps a gap invisible.
Node was also rejected because it cannot start npm.cmd or aspire.cmd on Windows, and land-ticket runs four npm commands.
It corrects the earlier record that said Loop's code is shell and node: it is shell and Python.
